data_structures.composite_key_max: 9 * 2 = 18 groups max (stmt dict has 9 entries, rfile dict has 2 entries)
data_structures.composite_key_note: CRITICAL: Do NOT use bit-shift (stmt << 8 | rfile) — stmt codes go up to 8, producing keys up to 2049 which overflows a 256-slot array. Use multiplication: stmt_code * num_rfile + rfile_code. Load num_rfile from rfile dictionary count at runtime.
data_structures.distinct_adsh: bitset per group: (max_adsh_code + 63) / 64 uint64_t words. max_adsh_code = adsh dict count = 86135, so 1346 words = 10768 bytes per group. With 18 groups per thread: 18 * (24 + 10768) = ~194KB per thread

parallelism.thread_local_state: each thread has its own flat array of (num_stmt * num_rfile) agg structs with bitsets, allocated via calloc inside parallel region
parallelism.total_note: 64 threads * 194KB = ~12MB total — fits comfortably in LLC

dictionaries.name: stmt
dictionaries.purpose: identify null sentinel code (code for empty string) and decode output, also get num_stmt = dict.count

dictionaries.name: rfile
dictionaries.purpose: decode output, also get num_rfile = dict.count

dictionaries.name: adsh
dictionaries.purpose: get max_adsh = dict.count for bitset sizing (only read the count, no need to decode strings)

optimization_notes: Category A — Plan restructuring. Root cause: iter_0 crashed (SIGSEGV) due to buffer overflow in composite key computation. The formula (stmt_code << 8) | rfile_code produces values up to 2049 (stmt has 9 dictionary codes 0-8), but only 256 array slots were allocated. Fix: use composite_key = stmt_code * num_rfile + rfile_code, giving max 9*2=18 groups. Allocate array sized to num_stmt * num_rfile at runtime. This also reduces per-thread memory from 2.76MB to 194KB (18 vs 256 groups), improving cache locality. Retained from iter_0: demand-paged mmap with MADV_SEQUENTIAL + MADV_HUGEPAGE, no MAP_POPULATE, schedule(static), no Kahan summation, mmap declared before RAII timer scope, per-group bitset for COUNT(DISTINCT adsh). For adsh dict, only read the uint32_t count from the first 4 bytes — no need to decode all 86K strings.
